The famous ship that sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg is the RMS Titanic.

To explain the complex concept of blockchain using an analogy: Imagine a community notebook where everyone writes down every transaction that happens in their village. Instead of keeping this notebook in one person's house (which could be lost, stolen, or altered secretly), every single family in the village keeps an identical copy of the same notebook.

When a new transaction occurs, it is announced to the whole village. Everyone checks their own notebook to verify that the transaction makes sense (for example, ensuring the person spending money actually has enough funds). Once the majority of families agree that the transaction is valid, they all write it down in their own notebooks at the same time.

Because every family has a copy, no single person can secretly change a past entry without everyone else noticing. If one person tries to erase a debt in their own notebook, the other thousands of notebooks will still show the debt, and the change will be rejected. This collective agreement and widespread copying make the record extremely secure and trustworthy, just like the decentralized digital ledger described in the evidence.
